## Changes
- **The first calculation after an update is no longer slow.** AURIS used to compile its calculation code on the first calculation after every update, which on P2003 took 202 s instead of 113 s. The calculation code now comes ready-compiled inside the app.
- **Old calculation caches are cleared.** Each version left about 34 MB behind. Caches no installed copy of AURIS uses are now deleted, and one still used by another installed copy is kept.

history.notes:
## Changes
- **Report-quality contours are 3 to 7 times faster.** Refining a grid now stops at cells a quarter of the grid spacing across (at most 1 m), instead of chasing detail down to 6 cm. Against exact levels at 1,500 random points per site, the drawn bands are just as accurate as before, and more accurate than an exact grid at 1 m. On a 4 m grid, P2003 now refines in 67 s instead of 8 minutes, and P1922 in 4.4 minutes instead of 13.
- **ISO 9613-2 calculations use 11 to 23% less processor time, with identical results.** The most gain is around reflecting buildings and barriers. P2003's full site at 1 m now takes 120 s instead of 132 s.

## Changes
- **SmartSmooth, rebuilt from the ground up.** Contours are drawn by a new engine, with reflections on or off, in plan and in section:
  - **Simplify now states its accuracy.** Each step allows the drawn field to differ from the calculated levels by at most 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 2 dB (Raw: none). Within that, it draws the smoothest contours possible. Features smaller than the allowance (spikes, needles, notches, stair-steps) go, and anything larger is kept.
  - **No more hairs or needles.** Simplify also sets the narrowest feature it keeps (up to 1.5 grid cells). A path switching on and off over a few centimetres, such as a reflection at a façade corner, is no longer drawn as a needle or a hairy edge. Raw still shows it.
  - **Smoothing follows the contours.** Close to a source, where contours are tight, smoothing reaches only a short way and they keep their shape. Far afield, where contours are wide apart, it reaches further, giving long, clean curves.
  - **Smooth curves, never stair-steps.** The calculated grid is interpolated with a smooth curve that never goes beyond its neighbouring points, and simplified contour lines lose the grid's stair-steps.
  - **Walls and barriers are exact.** Contours never pass through a building, barrier or court wall. Where the level jumps across a wall, the bands on each side run straight up to it, with no slivers or specks along the wall.
  - **Bands and lines always agree.** Every band boundary is a single shared line: no gaps, overlaps or crossings at any setting.
  - **Faster.** A style change on a large site takes about a second.
- **Building labels on the map show just the house number** when the building is named by its address ("160 Camden High Street" shows as "160"). The full name stays in the Inspector and in exports.
- **Calculations are slightly faster** (about 3% on area-source contour maps), with identical results.

## Bug fixes
- **SmartSmooth painted some areas in the wrong band.** On a section behind a tall building, the area beyond the roof was drawn as 15–20 dB where the calculated levels are 9–15 dB.
- **SmartSmooth on Simplify Extreme kept thin needles and spikes**, and showed notches and stair-stepped edges near buildings and where reflections switch on or off.

## Bug fixes
- **Contour maps had empty squares along the line of a façade source's wall.** Grid points that fell on the wall's line, beyond the building's end or past the source, received no sound at all, so the basemap showed through. They now have their proper level.
- **Too little sound round the corner of a building from a façade source.** The path round the corner of the source's own building was left out, so levels just behind the façade's line, beside the building, dropped by about 30 dB instead of a few dB. Recalculate contour maps and receptors that include façade sources.
- **Façade sources disappeared from contour sheets** when contours were shown: they were drawn under the contour colours. They now draw on top, like point sources.

## Changes
- **Edit façade panes directly in 3D.** Click a vertical area source (a window, louvre or door on a façade) and:
  - **Drag it** to slide it along its façade, or drag its top, bottom or ends to resize it. The cursor and a teal edge show what a drag will do. Panes snap to the ground, the roof line, the ends of the façade and the edges of neighbouring panes, otherwise to 5 cm, and never slip off their façade or below ground.
  - **Hold ⌥ and drag** to copy it (works for any area source).
  - In **Properties › Façade pane**, set the bottom height above ground, the pane height and its width, or click **Duplicate** to place a copy beside it.
  - **Array…** repeats it across or up the façade: choose the direction (right, left, up, down, or a grid), how many across and up, and the gap or centre-to-centre spacing. A preview shows the new panes on the façade before you create them; copies that would leave the façade or land on an existing pane are left out and listed.
- **Place search finds places anywhere.** Northern Ireland, Ireland, the rest of Europe and beyond now come up alongside Ordnance Survey's Great Britain results, with each place's region and country shown.
- **CRTN road calculations near many buildings are about 15% faster**, with identical results.

## Bug fixes
- **Searching for a place in Northern Ireland found nothing** when an Ordnance Survey key was set (Ordnance Survey covers Great Britain only).

## Changes
- **Calculations are much faster on most sites, with identical results.** Every grid level matches 0.42 exactly; the time saved comes from doing the same calculation with less work. Measured on the test sites and your projects (CPU time per grid point):
  - Padel courts: P2001 Dragon Padel about **6×** faster (a 31 s grid now takes 4.4 s); courts with glass rebound walls about 1.5×; P2003 about 1.3×.
  - ISO 9613-2 roads near many buildings about **4×** faster; line sources about 2×.
  - Industrial sites (point, line and area sources with reflections) about 2.3×; large area sources about 1.7×; parking areas about 1.4×.
- **Busy sites are no longer left on the slow route.** Sites with many buildings (over about 100) used a slower general-purpose path search; they now use the fast compiled one, which finds paths around buildings far more quickly.
- **Ground beyond the survey points is fast.** Grid points and sources outside the area covered by ground points (common where roads or the grid run past the survey) were evaluated in slow Python code; they are now handled by the compiled engine, giving the same heights.
- **Ground heights are found faster on detailed terrain**, for example around level court platforms.

## Bug fixes
- None in this release: it changes speed only.

## Changes
- **The 3D view runs on Metal on Apple silicon.** It used OpenGL, which macOS runs through a translation layer: orbiting now holds a steady 120 frames a second (it stuttered at about 60), and the renderer's full feature set is available. Other Macs keep OpenGL.
- **Four distinct render qualities.** Low is a flat technical look (no cast shadows), Medium adds sun shadows, High adds crisp soft-edged shadows and distance haze, and Ultra (Apple silicon) adds contact shadows and reflections and takes on the soft, luminous look of the Ultra quality render. Projects saved with Performance, High or Ultra open on Medium, High and Ultra.
- **Shadows are crisp at any zoom.** They no longer break into steps or wobble when you look closely: the shadow detail follows what the camera is looking at.
- **The Ultra quality render shows everything the 3D view does,** in its own soft daylight: basemaps and drawings, trees, contours, façade results, the court glass, and the view's haze. Distant ground fades and softens gently, as in real air, and the render is cleaner (no grain or speckles on walls).
- **Haze builds gradually with distance** from the point you are looking at, instead of starting beyond the whole site.
- **Padel courts look as built:** a blue playing surface on a concrete slab, black steel frame, glass that reads as glass, black mesh panels and a net with its white band.
- **A redesigned 3D toolbar.** Controls are grouped (navigate, camera, look, layers and façades), the display style, time of day and quality show their current setting, and Render has its own button.
- **Façade results calculate about twice as fast** (P2003's three buildings: 34 s to 14 s), with the same levels.

## Bug fixes
- **Edits made in the 2D editor did not always reach the 3D view,** for example a court's markings or level platform, or an area source's model. Every change now shows when you return to 3D.
- **Ground contours had holes** where sloping ground rose between the contour grid points; they now lie exactly on the ground. Smooth contour styles also have smooth band edges in 3D, and contour lines are drawn at a sensible width on the ground (a 4 pt line had become 4 m wide).
- **A padel court without a level platform had sloping ground showing through its surface.** The surface now follows the ground.
- **Ultra's ambient occlusion left black patches at the foot of walls.**
- **The Ultra quality render showed a different, broken scene:** no basemap or trees, opaque court glass and a streaked sky.

## Bug fixes
- **Courts on a level platform made calculations and contours extremely slow.** Every height on the platform and its slope was worked out one point at a time outside the fast calculation engine, so a contour map of a site with one levelled court ran about 200 times slower than without the platform. The platform is now built into the ground surface itself (the flat court, its apron and the slope back to natural ground), and these sites calculate at full speed again.
- **Levels with a court on a level platform were wrong.** Parts of the calculation used the platform and others the natural ground under it, so switching the platform on made a whole site about 1.5 dB quieter, even far from the court. Every part now uses the platform: away from the court it changes levels by less than half a decibel, as it should, and beside the court by up to about 1.5 dB where the ground and walls change. Recalculate projects with a level platform; measured courts are recalibrated automatically.
- **Switching on a court's glass walls froze AURIS for minutes when the court had a level platform.** Recalibrating the court was slow for the same reason, and it ran while the window waited. It now uses the fast engine, and switching the walls on takes about a second.
- **Refining contours sat at 97 % for most of the refinement.** The refinement found its receivers in several rounds; the first round filled the bar and the later rounds had nowhere left to go. Each round now fills part of the bar that is left, so the bar keeps moving.

## Bug fixes
- **Refining a contour map's detail sat at 85 % for the whole refinement.** Its first, short checks were counted as the end of the job. The bar now moves with the refined points, from start to finish.
- **Updating a contour map's look (bands, lines, smoothing) sat at 98 % until it finished.** The bar now follows each step of the SmartSmooth presentation, including building the contour mesh, which used to show no movement for several seconds.
- **Contour progress ran far ahead of or behind the clock on some sites.** Grid points are now handed out spread across the site, so the percentage keeps pace with the time taken. Results are unchanged, and calculations are slightly faster.
- **Opening a large older-format project showed no progress until it appeared.** The bar now moves while the project is read, and its pace for each stage is set by the file size.

## Changes
- **ISO 9613-2 contour maps are several times faster.** P2003's contour map needs about a sixth of the computing time it did (its area source with reflections was the slowest part), and sites with many buildings and barriers are about three times faster. The path calculations (screening, side paths round buildings, ground, terrain, reflections and area-source cells) now run as compiled code that does exactly the same arithmetic as before.
- **Repeat calculations give exactly the same result.** Some internal caches rounded positions to a thousandth of a millimetre, so a grid point's level could depend on which points happened to be calculated first, and two runs of the same model could differ very slightly. Results are now fully repeatable. Levels change by no more than 0.0000001 dB.
- **The first calculation after updating is no longer slow.** AURIS now prepares its compiled calculation code once in the background, at low priority, shortly after the first launch of a new version.
- **The update window lists every release you skipped**, newest first, instead of only the latest release's notes.

## Bug fixes
- **The contour progress bar sat at 85 % for the whole refinement stage.** It now moves with the refinement's actual progress.
- **Padel court frames cast shadows in 3D.** The thin court frames no longer cast shadows.

## Changes
- **CRTN contour maps are about five times faster.** P2000's contour map takes about 2 minutes instead of about 11. The heaviest CRTN geometry (ground heights along each path, terrain crests, building screening) now runs as compiled code that does exactly the same arithmetic, so every level is unchanged to the last digit. The first calculation after updating takes a few seconds longer while it compiles.

## Bug fixes
- **A sports court's LAFmax set to "Nearest plausible point" could come out far too low.** The ball strike was placed on the court edge, which can be the foot of the court's own glass end wall, so the wall screened it and LAFmax came out only a few dB above LAeq. The event is now placed at the nearest point in play (1 m inside the edge), and is never quieter than the event at the court centre.

## New features
- **The real sun.** In Daylight, the sun now stands where it really is over your site for the clock time, using the site's location and UK time (GMT or BST). Choose the day in Lighting: today, the spring or autumn equinox, midsummer or midwinter. The sun shows as a white disc with a soft bloom, and its shadows and light follow it.
- **Clear-day 3D look.** A deep blue sky with a pale horizon, bright white clay in sun and light cool-blue shade.
- **Haze you can set.** Aerial haze now lies on the ground and thins upward, so distant land fades while the sky stays clear. A Haze slider in Lighting sets how far it reaches; the far right turns it off.
- **Sports courts sit level on sloping ground.** A court placed on a slope is levelled at the ground height of the first point you click. The ground is flat across the court and a 1 m apron, then eases back to the natural ground on a gentle slope (cut or fill). The calculation, contours and 3D all use this ground, and it works over imported LiDAR/DTM grids. The Inspector's "Level platform on sloping ground" switches it on or off for any court.
- **Roads are locked in place.** Dragging a selected road no longer moves the whole road by accident: drag its nodes to reshape it, or use the move handle drawn beside the road to move all of it. Nodes and width handles only move once you have dragged a few pixels, so a click never nudges them.
- **QA comb.** `python -m qa comb` builds random and deliberately awkward sites and checks that every calculation route agrees with itself: repeatable levels, results unchanged when moved to national-grid coordinates, save and reload, contour grid against receptors, CRTN and ISO routes, and the plan and 3D builds.

## Changes
- **3D runs smoothly.** Orbiting P2000 went from about 18 to about 100 frames a second. While the camera moves, shadows draw at lower resolution; full-quality shadows return a moment after it stops.
- **Smoother 3D ground.** Terrain is sampled about every 2.5 m (it was every 12 m on large sites without a terrain grid) and shades smoothly instead of showing flat triangles.
- **Roads in 3D:** asphalt is grey rather than near-black, every central reservation carries the slim concrete barrier, and a ground-coloured strip below each kerb closes the gap where the sky showed through beside the road.
- **CRTN contour maps are nearly twice as fast** (P2000: about 26 to about 14 minutes), because work is spread evenly across all cores. Opposite-façade reflections are also quicker, with identical results.
- **Simplify and Smoothing apply in seconds** instead of up to a minute.
- **Contour updates are quicker:** the presentation mesh builds in half the time, band extraction no longer freezes the window, and switching palettes no longer re-samples every object's height.
- **Saves and autosave are more than twice as fast**, and autosave waits while a contour presentation is being built.
- **Receptors and point sources draw above outlines** such as the site boundary, so they stay visible and clickable.

## Bug fixes
- **3D now updates after you edit roads.** Moving a whole road and then deleting a node could stop later road edits reaching the saved road, so the 3D view and the CRTN calculation kept using the old road. Road edits now always carry through, and existing projects heal on opening.
- **Roads no longer float above the ground in 3D.**
- **A road below CRTN's flow range gives a clear message** naming the road and how to fix it (raise the flow, use CRTN + ISO 9613-2, or exclude the road), not a traceback.
- **CRTN no longer counts walls beside a railway as road reflectors.** With rail in a project, a receptor's road level could rise by up to 0.1 dB and disagree with the contour map at the same point.
- **A receptor or contour point exactly at a source no longer fails the whole calculation.** That point has no level and every other point calculates.
- **Calculations at national-grid coordinates** no longer stop on area-source subdivision or on a barrier seen edge-on from a receptor.
- **The first contour calculation on a new model covers what is on screen.** It solved a default 100 m area when started from the Editor.
- **Contours say "Preparing presentation" until the map is really ready**, instead of "ready" about 20 seconds early.
- **3D buildings meet undulating ground without gaps.**
- **The Inputs table** says a receptor level is "out of date (model changed)" instead of a cut-off phrase.

## New features
- **Edit a road's nodes and segments directly in the plan.** Selecting a road now shows just its centre nodes. Double-click a node or a segment to edit it: its width handles appear with the width written across the road, and a small bar beside it offers width, height and, for a segment, a Bridge switch. Drag one end of a segment to change that end, or hold Shift to keep both ends equal (Alt gives 1 cm steps). Alt-click adds or removes a node, Delete removes the selected node and Esc finishes. The same actions are on the road's right-click menu.
- **Set road heights the way you think about them.** Raise or lower a node or segment relative to its normal height (the default when the project has terrain), as a height above the ground, or as an absolute level. Raised or lowered road still builds an embankment or cutting that follows it.
- **Bridges per segment.** Switch Bridge on for just the segment that crosses another road or a valley. A bridge segment runs straight between its nodes and leaves the ground below untouched. If a bridge deck would pass below the ground between its nodes, the Inspector says so.

## Changes
- **A clearer road Inspector.** One overall width sits next to the road type; dual carriageways and motorways add both carriageway widths and the reservation on one row. Fields sit two or three to a row when the panel is wide enough, the section for the selected node or segment opens by itself, and the detailed per-node table, carriageway geometry, calibration and project settings stay folded away until needed. Choosing a road type now applies its widths to the whole road.
- **Full screen uses the standard macOS title bar**, dark in Dark Mode, and the extra space around the menus eases in instead of jumping.
- **Updates install inside AURIS** even when it was started from source, into the copy in Applications.

## Bug fixes
- **A road marked as a bridge no longer runs inside a hill.** A bridge running end to end along a hillside road sat up to 5 m below the ground; a bridge now never dips below the ground at its interior nodes.
- **Dragging a dual carriageway's width no longer turns it into a single carriageway.** Each node keeps at least two 3 m carriageways plus the reservation.
- **CRTN emission with ISO 9613-2 propagation keeps both carriageways of a dual road whose width varies.** It had combined them into one centre line; full CRTN was not affected.
- **The red source lines follow the true kerbs** in the plan and 3D where a road's width varies.
- **Single-track roads have no centre line**, and the central barrier of a dual carriageway is galvanised steel in 3D rather than black.

## Changes
- **Interpolated Raster is ready sooner again.** On a 250-building padel project with sloping ground, contour support refinement now takes about 35 s instead of 57 s in 0.38.0. Calculated levels are unchanged: validation grids are bit-identical, and refined levels agree to within a trillionth of a decibel.
- **What made the difference:** area sources are subdivided (ISO 9613-2 Clause 4) and lateral path lengths (7.4.3) worked out by compiled code that reproduces the previous arithmetic exactly; unscreened source–receiver pairs skip the barrier search entirely; terrain and building-seam checks run in batches; and the refinement worker pool starts while the grid is still being partitioned.

## Changes
- **Contour grids calculate several times faster, with the same results.** On a 250-building padel project with sloping ground, a 4 m Raw grid now takes 14 s instead of 89 s, and a 2 m grid 52 s instead of over 4 minutes. Calculated levels match the previous version to within a billionth of a decibel.
- **Interpolated Raster is ready about six times sooner.** Its contour support refinement takes under a minute instead of seven to eight on the same project, and the interpolated bands draw in half the time, with identical band boundaries.
- **What made the difference:** lateral paths round buildings (ISO 9613-2 7.4.3) are found with a much better-guided search that still returns the exact shortest route, and building visibility is worked out once instead of for every few receivers. Ground profiles are sampled only where the terrain could reach the ray, and refinement now uses every processor core to the end of each pass.

## Bug fixes
- **Courts emitting at the contour height no longer leave missing squares around them.** The court's own outline is left blank, and the bands now run up to it and fill the gaps between courts, instead of dropping whole grid cells.

## New features
- **Breakout sources from a building.** In a building's Indoor sound level section, enter the façade and roof transmission losses and choose Create breakout sources: AURIS adds one pane per façade, from the ground to the roof, standing 50 mm off the wall and radiating outwards, plus a roof source, all using the building's indoor level (ISO 12354-4 with ISO 9613-2 outdoors). Run it again after changing the building and it replaces the panes it created.
- **Build up a transmission loss from its elements.** Build up… takes a wall's elements (wall, windows and doors by area and R, trickle vents and other small elements by count and Dn,e) and gives the composite R', as one value or per band, for a building's breakout or any breakout pane.
- **Input sensitivity.** Results › More › Input sensitivity… changes one input at a time on a copy of the scenario (hard or porous ground, meteorological correction, reflections, air conditions, buildings and barriers higher or lower, sources higher) and recalculates. It also ranks every source by what a ±3 dB change in its sound power does to each receptor, worked out exactly from its share of the level. The results show as a chart for each receptor, with a CSV export for an appendix.

## Changes
- **Rotate a multiple selection.** A selection of several objects now has its own rotate grip above its box and turns about the box's centre. Hold Shift to snap to the drawing angle step. Directional sources turn with it, and it is one undo step.

## Bug fixes
- **Model checks no longer report vertical panes as zero-area.** A pane is measured by its wall area, not its footprint on plan.

## New features
- **Why this level? shows every term per source.** Each source's distance, geometrical divergence, air absorption, ground and screening (of its strongest element) and its reflections sit beside its contribution.
- **Paths, in plan and in section.** Select an element in Why this level? › Details › Paths to see how its sound reaches the receptor: the direct line (dashed where screened), the diffraction edges, the lateral paths round buildings (faint where ISO 9613-2 rejects them), reflections and the nearby buildings, with the over-the-top path in section and its Abar.
- **Export the calculation protocol.** Every emitting element's position, sound power, distance, Adiv, Aatm, Agr, Abar, Amisc, Cmet, reflections and contribution, then the energy sum reconciled with the stored result, as a spreadsheet for a technical appendix.
- **Independent benchmarks in the validation centre.** Help › Standards validation now also checks the engine against references it did not produce: spherical divergence with the ISO 9613-2 ground image, sound power to receiver level, energetic summation, area sources against a 40,000-cell integration near and far, the ProPG padel calibration (LAeq 60 dB and LAFmax 71 dB at 5 m), and maxima kept apart from LAeq, each with its stated tolerance.
- **Model checks that catch modelling mistakes**: sources or receptors inside buildings, duplicate sources on the same spot (+3 dB), courts without an LAFmax, a court's measurement position inside a building, areas emitting at the contour height, and courts that would calculate several times faster at their centre point.

## Changes
- **Padel courts in 3D look like padel courts**: a blue playing surface (the plan keeps the source colour), slim posts at the panel joints tied by rails, see-through glass and a net with its white top band.
- **Selections read at a glance.** What a selection box will select is outlined in teal as you drag it, every object of a multiple selection keeps a teal outline, and the selection box follows the objects' own direction.
- **Cursors say what a click will do**: a pointing hand over an object you can select, an open hand over a selected object you can move, the fine reticle on corners and edges, and a rotate cursor on the rotation grip.
- **Rotating is smooth.** Receptor stacks, contours, live levels and 3D update once when the rotation ends, not on every mouse move. Hold Shift to rotate in whole steps of the drawing angle snap (15° by default).
- **The ⌘/Ctrl distance guide always starts** when placing receptors or sources, even straight after choosing the tool from the toolbar.

## Bug fixes
- **Interpolated contours complete for courts emitting at the contour height.** A 1.5 m court on a 1.5 m contour plane failed with "Nonfinite exact propagation-region support" (ISO 9613-2 has no level on an emitting surface), and the contours were left interpolating the bare grid, which scalloped shadow boundaries. The court's own footprint is left blank instead.

## Changes
- **Installing from the disk image replaces AURIS in Applications.** Open AURIS from the installer window and it offers to install itself over the copy in Applications (projects and settings are kept), then opens it and ejects the disk image. Dragging to Applications made Finder ask to Replace or Keep Both, and failed while AURIS was open.
- **LAFmax is entered as it is measured**, at a distance, for every source type (a court: beside it, as ProPG measures), whatever basis its LAeq uses. The Inspector shows the event sound power it gives.
- **Where an area's maximum event happens is explicit:** at the reference-calibrated centre (a court's default, so the model reproduces the LAFmax measured beside it), at the nearest plausible point to each receptor (other areas' default), or placed at a known position. Max levels names the governing source per receptor and lists each source's events in its tooltip and basis sheet.
- **Maxima of independent sources do not add**: the highest single event counts. Simultaneous events (energies added) are a deliberate choice in Max levels.
- **C or Z weighting does not relabel an A-weighted maximum**: broadband LAFmax stays LAFmax, with a note.
- **Library court records state the court's own size and area** with its sound power (a 20 x 6 m singles court has a higher density per m² than a doubles court from the same record).
- **Receptor tables** band by building instead of by row, keep names level with their first floor, and say a shared sound field once in the summary instead of on every row.

## Bug fixes
- **Measured courts are calibrated at a reference site.** A court's measured level (typed, or from ProPG) becomes sound power with the court, its own glass walls and the ground only. Before, the site's own buildings counted: a building at one P2005 court's measurement position, 5 m beside it, made that court 20 dB too loud and raised receptors 120 m away by about 11 dB. Courts recalibrate when a project opens.
- **Max levels show maximum levels.** With All scenarios selected, the Max levels tab showed the LAeq comparison under its name. Assessments now use the open scenario, and maxima recalculate when the model changes. A source without a maximum has none; its LAeq is never used.
- **No crash in the Emission library list.** Refreshing the list of library records could crash AURIS.
- **"Why this level?" works when comparing scenarios**, for the level selected (it was hidden there, and Calculate all scenarios ends on the comparison).

## New features
- **BS 4142 period by period.** Results › BS 4142 keeps a background LA90 for each period, and the character corrections are shared until a period takes its own (for example +3 dB for intermittency at night only). Excel exports get one sheet and basis per period, and the initial estimate appears as a pill.
- **BS 4142 › All periods.** Every period's background, rating level and initial estimate side by side, with a headline per period. A column of measured backgrounds copied from a spreadsheet pastes straight into the Background cells.
- **Emission, reworked.** One question comes first, Level from: Sound power, Sound pressure (Measured for courts), Library, plus Moving plant for lines and Breakout for areas. Only the fields that answer needs follow. Sound pressure takes LpA with its distance and radiation Q, and an LAFmax that becomes the event sound power.
- **A library that knows what fits.** The Library choice only offers records that apply to the selected object, each with a one-line summary.
- **ProPG Sport & Leisure data.** Padel (tables 13.25 and 13.26) and football (tables 13.3 to 13.7) source records, measured beside the court or behind its end, sit in the library.
- **Measured courts calibrate against the model.** A level beside a court or behind its end, typed or from ProPG, becomes sound power through the model's own response at the measurement position (ground, terrain, screens and reflections). The model then reproduces the measured LAeq there on any ground; free-field spreading alone was 3 dB out either way between hard and porous ground. Max levels place the court's event at its centre.
- **Courts at their centre (CadnaA).** A court can be one point at its centre and height, as CadnaA models padel ("Padel – Center of Court"), and new padel courts start that way. On a five-court padel site, eight receivers took 7.6 s instead of 192 s.
- **Glass rebound walls are a switch** on a padel court ("Glass walls screen sound"). The walls follow the court when it moves or turns, and are removed with it.
- **Padel courts in 3D, as built.** The glass ends and returns, mesh above and along the sides with a gate either side of the net, posts, the net, and the court surface with its markings on the ground.
- **A clay look in 3D**, matched to architectural clay model renders: high-key and soft, with lavender shade, soft-edged sun shadows, ambient occlusion that grounds buildings, rounded building edges, and a sky that follows the time of day (pale by day, warm at dawn and dusk, deep blue at night).
- **Depth of field in 3D.** A switch in the Lighting popover focuses on the point the view orbits and softens the foreground and distance, giving the miniature look of a model photographed close up (perspective views).
- **Save Ultra quality render.** A path-traced image with soft global illumination, refined for about a minute at up to twice the view's size, with progress, time left and Cancel. The rest of the app stays responsive while it renders.
- **Calculate all scenarios runs in the background** with receiver progress, and Stop works immediately.

## Changes
- **Period presets read Assessment Period and BS 4142**, with the details in tooltips. BS 4142's periods are plain Day and Night with their 1 h and 15 min lengths, which sheets show as LAeq,1h and LAeq,15min. A caution appears when a period's length is not the standard's reference interval.
- **Faster calculations around reflective screens.** Area sources next to reflective barriers do much less redundant work, with identical levels. On the same padel site a 4,800-point contour took 72 s.
- **Faster map import.** Names come in one Overpass request, objects are built while the image and terrain download, and roads are added in one batch.
- **Inspector rows pair up.** Name sits with Height, Input level with Max event, and Reference distance with Q. Each field keeps its own visibility per object type and goes full width when its partner is hidden.

## Changes
- **Road (CRTN/CRN) contours are now smooth and accurate in Interpolated, Gradient and SmartSmooth.** These projects skipped the extra calculation that adds receivers along shadows and barriers, so the smooth methods could only blend the coarse grid: shadows looked pixellated with a blur, and contours scalloped along barriers. They now get it too, and every barrier is a hard edge in the field. On a test model the result matches exact CRTN calculations within 0.1 dB. Calculation takes longer with a smooth method selected (P1930 at 4 m: about 50 s to 2 minutes); Raw is unchanged.

## Bug fixes

- The window's rounded corners could show a dark rim, more visible when AURIS was not the active window.

## Changes
- **SmartSmooth Simplify and Smoothing now work in sequence, as two clear steps.** Simplify turns each contour into a cleaner polygon, and each step on the slider looks visibly stronger: Extreme is deliberately faceted, so long road contours become clean straight runs. The amount follows each contour's own size, so tight rings near a source and long bands far from it are simplified to the same look; small rings are no longer flattened while large bands barely change. Smoothing then rounds the corners of that simplified shape with Bézier curves. At 100% it draws true arcs through the corners, and lower settings soften them less. Before, turning Smoothing on traced the raw contour again and could make lines more detailed instead of smoother.
- **Pick from screen samples any window or app** with the macOS colour loupe. It no longer needs Screen & System Audio Recording permission or a restart.
- The status bar's "Saved / Unsaved changes" check runs after you edit, instead of every second, which keeps AURIS responsive on large projects.

- **The splash after an update no longer freezes (beachball).** The font list used for plots was rebuilt after every update on the main thread, holding the splash for several seconds. It is now kept between updates, and when it does have to be built, the splash keeps moving.

## New features

Teal is the result on screen, white tiles are calculated, amber means the inputs have changed since, and empty tiles are not calculated yet. Click any tile to show that result. The Calculate button's second half is now **All**: every scenario and time slice, all time slices of this scenario, all scenarios for this time slice, or all views. Hover a choice to see which tiles it covers. During the run the tiles fill as they're calculated and the grid counts down ("Calculating 3 of 4 · about 2 min left"), then AURIS returns to the result you started on. Each scenario's results are saved, so they're all there when you reopen the project.
- **Interpolated contours keep fading shadow edges sharp.** Where a building's acoustic shadow fades out partway across an area, the level step along its edge no longer blends into neighbouring grid cells: each side takes its values from its own receivers, and beyond the point where the step fades, the field joins up smoothly again. Checked against 2,500 exact calculations on P1995, the field near these edges is closer to the true levels: average error 0.12 → 0.10 dB, and 90% of points within 0.20 dB (was 0.30 dB). Elsewhere it is unchanged.

## Changes
- **The SmartSmooth curve-smoothing slider now does what it says.** At 25%, 50% and 100% the curves follow the calculated contour progressively more loosely, within the same accuracy limits. Before, all three settings drew almost the same lines.

## New features
- **Sound events per time slice (SEL).** Point, line and area sources can now be continuous, a number of discrete events, or off in each time slice. Describe one event by its sound exposure (LwE, or SEL measured at a distance; a pass-by for a line) and, optionally, its LAFmax. AURIS turns N events in the slice into the equivalent continuous level, which receptors, contours and spectra use. The Inspector shows a live readout, for example "40 events → equivalent LwA 83.4 dB over the period". Projects from earlier versions are unchanged.
- **LAFmax for line sources with pass-by events.** The maximum is placed at the line's nearest point to each receptor and propagated with the same ISO 9613-2 route. A source that is off or excluded in the active slice no longer contributes a maximum.

## Changes
- **Soft elevation everywhere.** Settings, panels and switchers use one wide, soft, low-contrast shade instead of stacked hard rings.
- **Straight shadow edges in Interpolated contours.** Where a building's acoustic shadow begins, levels step by about 5 dB. Interpolated mode drew those steps as a sawtooth because many shadow lines stopped a fraction short of a building corner or a neighbouring line, so the contour blended straight across the step. These near-misses are now closed. On P1995 the share of shadow-line length that separates the field went from 50% to 77%, and the edges are drawn straight.
- **SmartSmooth fits smooth curves to each contour** instead of rounding the corners of a simplified polygon. That removes straight chords across arcs, bulges and hooks at building ends. Where a curve would break a safety check (usually a few metres beside a shadow edge or a building), only that stretch now stays close to the calculated line. Previously the whole line did, which made the 100% setting look less smooth than 25%. P1995 at 8 m: largest shift at the default settings 3.1 m → 0.5 m, and each slider change rebuilds faster (2.5 s → 1.8 s).
- **Contour refinement spends its receivers along features.** Areas the refinement could not afford in one pass stay in line for the next, and the cells beside a failed area are checked next. This gives even detail along diffraction edges instead of isolated 0.5 m patches beside untouched 8 m cells.
- **The contour progress bar follows the real work.** With buildings, most of the time goes into screening transitions, so the bar no longer races to 55% on the grid and then crawls.
- **The status-bar progress glides** like the dialog bars. Copy and Export on the contour sheet confirm with a tick (Copied / Saved) instead of a dialog, Copy Table confirms on its button, and secondary buttons show a clear hover and pressed state.

- The original AURIS teal is back as the default, and the top bar shows workspace icons only, as before 0.24.0.
- Settings is calmer: no outlines around cards, the sidebar, the search field or the selected item; cards sit on the soft app grey with a light shade instead of bright white, and the title bar now blends with the window.
- Clicking the Project / Preferences switch or Done no longer leaves a highlight ring (the ring still shows when you move through Settings with Tab).
- The Editor's start card says a map is optional and leads with *Continue without a map*, which hides it for the session.

## Bug fixes
- Import map data closed the app. The installer carried a second copy of the web engine without its helper process, and the map view loaded that copy. The build now keeps one complete copy (the app is about 227 MB smaller) and its release check opens a web page before shipping.

## New features
- **Start card on an empty project.** A new project opens with a short card on the canvas: import the site from map data, open a project, or pick a drawing tool. The grid stays drawable around it, and the card goes once the model has anything in it.
- **Workspace names in the top bar.** The Editor, Inputs, 3D View, Results and Contours switch shows each workspace's name beside its icon.

## Changes
- **Colours meet WCAG AA contrast in light and dark.** The interactive teal is a deeper tone, so white text on teal buttons reads at 5:1 (it was 2.4:1). Teal text, muted text, warnings, errors, the Saved/Unsaved chip, the dark-mode Save button and the focus ring all reach the AA minimums. The AURIS logo and contour colours are unchanged, and dark mode uses the white logo.
- The inspector shows each value once. Buildings, barriers and berms have one Height field (two showed the same value at different precisions); the ID is no longer repeated in the header and body; labels have no trailing colons, as in every other panel.
- The inspector header shows the same icon as the object's drawing tool instead of a two-letter code.
- Checkboxes in lists, trees and tables (3D objects, time-slice sources) show an empty box when off.
- Unavailable inspector buttons look unavailable.
- Vertex tables no longer cut off their "Base (m)" and "Height (m)" headers.
- The receptor stack list marks the selected receptor.
- Inputs lists sources and roads first, then receptors, then barriers and buildings. A receptor without a level says "not calculated".
- Results no longer repeats the scenario name on every row (exports keep it). A numeric last column (Margin) stays beside its header.
- The live preview menu says what it sets ("Preview: Balanced") and drops Auto, which sampled exactly as Balanced.
- Compliance Profile lists its locked assumptions in plain terms, as Settings names them.
- The Acoustic Probe names source types in words and shows the sum of its contributions.
- Unhide All Buildings moves to ⇧⌘H: ⌘H is macOS's Hide AURIS.

## Bug fixes
- A barrier height typed into the barrier panel and then saved or calculated without pressing Return was lost.
- Opening a project after visiting Results showed "not run yet" although the project had saved runs.
- One road with a measured LA10 input made every road's inspector show "Road preparation requires review" with no fields. Each road now opens the editor for its own method.
- The Acoustic Probe calculated each source's contribution on the ISO route even for CRTN roads and CRN railways, so the rows did not add up to the exact level (60.6 dB against 63.96 dB on one model). Contributions now use the same method as the total and add up to it.
- A line source's "LpA at 10 m" is a level in dB, not dB/m.
- Inspector panels that cannot grow (the road traffic editor) sat in the middle of spare height, leaving a gap under the header.

## New features
- **Live receptor levels follow receptor drags on slow models.** Moving a receptor now re-solves only that receptor's stack and keeps every other level, with identical numbers. On P1987 (three CRTN roads) each step takes about 2 s instead of 14 s. A change too slow to follow while you edit (moving a building on that model, for example) is skipped with a note in the status bar; live levels no longer switch off for the whole project.
- **Results says when a run is out of date.** When the model or calculation method has changed since the run on screen, a note above the table says so, as the Contours tab already does, so older levels are not reported by mistake.

- Scale bars put the last number on its tick with the unit after it, so "25 m" no longer crowds "20".
- The Inputs table spells out heights and thicknesses, and lists a building's courtyards only when it has some.

Opening another project, or turning View › Live Receptor Levels on again, tries again.

  - Import CAD / GIS Layers: each layer's choices sit neatly in their row with room for their values, and Height (m) is greyed out while a column supplies the height.

## Bug fixes
- A rare crash risk is removed: Python could tidy up memory on a background calculation thread and free screen objects there (the test suite crashed this way). Memory is now tidied only on the main thread, between events.
- The Time Slices preset box always showed "Day + Evening + Night", whatever the project's periods.

## New features
- **Live receptor levels while you edit.** Move a source or receptor, or change an object in the Inspector, and each receptor in view shows its level and the change your edit makes (52.3 ▲1.2), updating as you drag and fading a few seconds after the last edit. The change is measured against the model just before the edit, by the same calculation, and the levels equal Calculate exactly. Facade floors share one tag (the loudest floor) and tags never overlap; the receptors your edit changes most keep theirs. Nothing is saved as a result. View › Live Receptor Levels turns it off.
- **Colour-blind-safe and print palettes.** Three new contour colour presets: Viridis and Cividis (perceptually even and readable with colour-vision deficiency) and Greyscale (print). In all three, louder is always darker, so the scale reads without relying on hue.
- **Inputs and Results explain themselves when empty.** Inputs shows what the tab is for, three steps, and buttons to open the Editor or import map or CAD data. Results lists what is in place and what is missing (sources and roads, receptors, the calculation), with Calculate ready once the model can be calculated.
- **Level bars in Results.** Each level has a soft bar beside it, scaled within its column, so the loudest receptors stand out at a glance; the column maximum is in semibold.

## Changes
- **Faster SmartSmooth contours.** Contour thresholds are now traced on each face's own part of the fine lattice instead of the whole site for every face. On P1995 (Glasgow Road, 2 m grid) a full contour calculation takes 302 s instead of 452 s; tracing the thresholds takes 3 s instead of 142 s. The contours are identical.
- **Smaller projects with uploaded plans and images.** Uploaded basemaps (plans, screenshots, pasted images) are stored as lossless WebP: every pixel is kept and they take about a third less space (the uploads in ten recent projects: 226 MB → 145 MB). Existing basemaps are left as they are.
- **Assessment presets in two rows.** Settings › Calculation shows the General and Road traffic presets on separate, labelled rows: one of each can match at once, which looked like a conflict when they shared a row.
- **Why this level?** names the receptor beside the run, and for a run made by an earlier version of AURIS it says so and offers Calculate all scenarios instead of showing empty charts.
- Clearer Contours hint: "Inputs have changed since this result. Update Grid to recalculate Day."
- **Solid tool icons.** Every drawing-tool icon is now a solid shape with cut-out detail, like the 3D tab's icons, drawn at the exact size and sharpness of your screen. The point, line and area source icons are unchanged. The hand and pointer are redrawn, and the parking sign is a true sign blue with the P cut out.
- **One toolbar height everywhere.** The Contours tab's switchers and buttons are now 36 px like the Editor and 3D tabs, and options that are on show white on a solid teal tile, as in the other tabs.
- **Softer, fuller shadows** on the Update | All views and Export | Copy buttons: a true blur that fades away completely, with a soft top light.
- Map Import and Upload Basemap are blue again.
- The Project / Inspector panel has no outline, like the map beside it.
- The Search objects field is flat with a search glyph and proper spacing.
- Results: the receptor column no longer opens a wide gap before the levels, and empty-table tools are hidden until there are results.

## Bug fixes
- **Section shadow lines from a source off the section plane.** On oblique sections, barrier and roof shadow lines were often missing (about one section in five in our checks) and some were drawn where there was no change in visibility. Each line now follows the exact shadow of the barrier crest or roof edge, uses the barrier's real thickness, and stops where that edge stops casting the shadow.
- Undo now covers basemap alignment (Align m E/N: a run of nudges is one step), drawing a red-line outline and clearing red lines.
- Settings controls were 30 px instead of the 28 px of their grid, so combos and number boxes did not line up with the colour and switch controls.
- Results level bars ran under the longer numbers.
- The Contours tab logged "Unbalanced save/restore" painter warnings while painting section overlays.
- Switching between Bands and Gradient made the colour strip and the controls around it jump; the Colour blend row now eases in and out and nothing else moves.
- The contours on/off button showed a grey face in dark mode.

## New features
- **Dark mode** (Settings › Preferences › General › Appearance, or ⌘K › Switch to dark mode). The new appearance spreads across the window in a circle. AURIS remembers the choice on this Mac. Contour sheets stay white paper in both modes, and contour colours never change.
- **Search commands with ⌘K.** Type part of any menu command, drawing tool, tab or setting and press Return: "rep" finds Report Pack, "bar" the Barrier tool. Shortcuts are shown, and unavailable commands say so. Also in View › Search Commands.
- **Why this level?** (Results › Why this level?): a receptor's sources ranked by their share of the total, with what each would change if removed or made 3 dB quieter. Below, a waterfall shows how the selected source reaches the receptor: sound power, distance, air absorption, ground, screening, reflections and Cmet, each bar in dB. Every number reconciles exactly with the stored result.
- **Optimise barrier height** (barrier Inspector, or Project › Optimise Barrier Height…). Choose the receptors to protect and the level to reach. AURIS finds the least barrier area that meets it, as level panels, using the full calculation, and shows the trade-off between barrier area and level. Apply the heights as one undo step.
- **CAD and GIS layers.**
  - File › Import CAD / GIS Layers… reads DXF, GeoPackage and Shapefile. For each layer, choose what it becomes (buildings, barriers, roads, receptors, sources, foliage) and which column holds height and name.
  - File › Export › CAD / GIS Layers… writes the model, receptor levels and the current contour lines (each with its level) as GeoPackage, DXF or Shapefiles, in British National Grid coordinates when the project is on the map.
  - DWG is a closed format: export DXF from the CAD package.
- **New Project from Postcode** (File menu). Type a postcode or address: AURIS starts a new project and opens map import at the site with imagery, terrain, buildings with heights, roads, barriers and building names ticked. Confirm the area and press Import.
- **Edit in 3D.** Press and drag the selected source or receptor to move it, or the selected building's roof to change its height. Dragging anywhere else still orbits the view. Each edit is one undo step.
- **Section planes in 3D:** contour sections show as translucent panels.
- **Hover cards:** in Select mode, resting the pointer on a source, receptor, building or barrier shows its name and key values (sound power, level, height) without clicking.
- **Project notes.** The project's Description is now Project notes: a notepad for everyone working on the project. "+ Dated note" starts a new entry headed with the date, time and your name, so each consultant's notes stay attributable. Notes are not printed on sheets or reports.

## New features
- **Settings › Reflections › Ignore nearer than / Fade in up to.** This works like CadnaA's minimum receiver–reflector distance. Reflections from a wall closer to the receiver than the minimum are left out, then build up gradually to full strength by the fade distance. This removes the level step beside façades in contour maps. It is off by default, which follows ISO 9613-2 exactly. Existing results stay current until you use it.
- **Section markers on/off:** a new button in the Sheet toolbar shows or hides every section line on the plan sheet at once. The View menu's eye buttons still set them one by one.
- When an updated AURIS has been installed while the old copy is still open, AURIS says so and offers to save and reopen in the new version.

## Changes
- **Reflections reviewed:** contours and receptor results with reflections on were checked at orders 1, 2 and 3 on a dense terraced site. Contour grid points match independent receptor calculations exactly (0.0 dB difference at 40 points, including steep edges), and each higher order only adds energy, never removes it.
- **Connected buildings and barriers reflect as one surface.** Verified: a building or barrier split into touching pieces gives the same result as one piece, to 0.01 dB, at orders 1 and 2. Party walls between touching buildings never reflect.
- Straight-edged wedges and beams in contours with reflections are expected. Each reflection is heard only where a mirror image of the source can be seen through the wall. CadnaA's image-source method behaves the same way.
- With the **Raw calculated grid** method, each grid cell is drawn as a square, so edges at an angle to the grid look stepped. For report contours, use SmartSmooth.

## Bug fixes
- **Sound leaked through hairline gaps between adjoining buildings.** Traced or imported terraces often leave slits of a few millimetres between party walls. AURIS treated the two sides as separate objects and let sound pass straight through a 1 cm slit. Behind the terrace this gave levels up to 22 dB too high, as narrow streaks in contour maps, with or without reflections. Footprints within 4 cm of each other now screen as one object, exactly as touching ones do. Real gaps, such as alleys, still let sound through. Results behind such terraces can drop. On the review site, levels fell by up to 1.3 dB, and never rose by more than 0.1 dB.
- **Clicking a source could select the receptor next to it.** Sources and receptors were clickable well beyond their symbols, about three times the symbol size. Clicks now select exactly the symbol under the pointer.
- **3D view: clicking an object selects it and opens its parameters**, with or without the side panel showing. Clicks no longer pick a large area source, road or diagonal barrier whose invisible bounding box happened to lie under the pointer.
- If the fast contour solver could not start, AURIS silently fell back to a much slower path. It now records this in the log.
- **SmartSmooth could not finish on dense terraced sites, and could exhaust the Mac's memory.** Along a terrace, dozens of building corners lie almost on one façade line. Every pair of them produced its own copy of the same shadow boundary, a fraction of a millimetre to a few millimetres apart: 42,140 copies on the review site. SmartSmooth checked each copy with extra calculations, then tried to fit the whole bundle into its contour mesh. That used 60+ GB and the calculation was killed after about 26 minutes. Copies within 5 mm are now treated as one boundary, well inside SmartSmooth's centimetre accuracy. On the review site, SmartSmooth now completes in about 2 minutes at reflection orders 1 and 2 and under 4 minutes at order 3, peaking at about 6 GB. Its smoothed field passes exactly through every calculated grid point (0.0 dB difference at 96,262 nodes).
- SmartSmooth sends far fewer progress updates from its boundary search (about 1,500 instead of 24,000 on a dense terrace), which also makes that stage a little faster.
